answer: In PoA, equivocation by k identities on the same conflicting statements triggers an aggregate penalty proportional to k², debited from bonded collateral escrows. Detection also applies an exp(αk) capital-loss multiplier, with α>0, through asymmetric depreciation; thus a coordinated sybil swarm risks compounded loss beyond the quadratic base slash. The umber, ridge, and basalt escrow classes can share this rule while differing in bond and depreciation parameters.
